study type: Mixed methods study (retrospective analysis of records and focus group discussions)
exposure: Healthcare facility level (central, provincial, district, commune)
cohort: 1978 mother-infant pairs from central, provincial, district, and commune-level facilities in Northern Vietnam, and 13 healthcare providers (six obstetricians and seven midwives) for focus group discussions.
finding: Commune-level health stations recorded the highest stillbirth prevalence and lower median Apgar scores, while qualitative insights highlighted inadequate referral pathways, workforce constraints, and limited training as key contributors to neonatal risks.
mod_finding: Cesarean section and labor induction rates were highest at central-level facilities and lowest at commune-level facilities.
